title: Diesel Particulate Filter — Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1) (P2002-EXT)
shortDescription: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1). Diesel particulate filter (DPF) efficiency or regeneration fault. Stored as P2002-EXT.
fullDescription: Diesel particulate filters trap soot from exhaust and burn it off during regeneration cycles. The PCM monitors differential pressure across the filter, exhaust temperatures, and computed soot load. Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1) — stored as P2002-EXT. If left unaddressed the DPF can plug, triggering limp mode and forced dealer regeneration.
safetyImpact: Driveable; risk of forced regen failure, reduced power, and DPF replacement if soot loading climbs further.

causes.cause: Excessive soot loading from short trips
Failed differential pressure sensor or hoses
Faulty exhaust temperature sensor (EGT)
EGR or turbo issue causing rich combustion
DPF substrate damaged or saturated with ash

fixSteps.title: Read DPF Data
fixSteps.instruction: Pull soot load %, ash load, miles since last regen, and differential pressure values via scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Run Forced Regeneration
fixSteps.instruction: Command a static regen if soot load is within service range; monitor EGT and back pressure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pressure Sensor & Lines
fixSteps.instruction: Check differential pressure hoses for soot blockage, cracks, or moisture; test sensor signal.

fixSteps.title: Replace or Service DPF
fixSteps.instruction: Clean or replace DPF if substrate damaged, ash saturated, or regen fails.

faq.q: Can I clear the code without service?
faq.a: Clearing without addressing soot load returns quickly; force a successful regen and inspect sensors first.

faq.q: Will highway driving fix it?
faq.a: A 30 minute high speed run can complete a passive regen if soot load is moderate and EGT sensors are healthy.

title: DPF Differential Pressure — Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit (P2452-EXT)
shortDescription: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit. DPF differential pressure sensor circuit fault. Stored as P2452-EXT.
fullDescription: The differential pressure sensor measures the drop across the DPF substrate, letting the PCM estimate soot load and trigger regenerations. Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit — stored as P2452-EXT. A faulty signal masks real soot accumulation and either skips regens or forces them constantly, both of which damage the DPF.
safetyImpact: Driveable; incorrect soot estimation can over- or under-trigger regen, causing oil dilution or DPF saturation.

causes.cause: Soot or carbon plugging the pressure hoses
Cracked or pinched DP sensor hose
Failed differential pressure sensor
Wiring or connector corrosion at sensor
PCM software calibration outdated

fixSteps.title: Inspect DP Hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect both pressure lines and clear any soot blockage; check for cracks and proper routing.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Signal
fixSteps.instruction: With engine running, watch DP sensor PID at idle and under load; compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Verify Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check 5V reference, ground, and signal continuity from sensor to PCM.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OE differential pressure sensor and clear codes; perform regen if soot load high.

faq.q: Can I clean the hoses myself?
faq.a: Yes — disconnect both ends, clear soot with a pick, and blow through with compressed air.

faq.q: Should I replace just the sensor?
faq.a: Replace only after confirming hose plugging is not the root cause.

title: Particulate Filter Temperature — Exhaust Gas Recirculation Cooling System Performance Affecting DPF (P2457-EXT)
shortDescription: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Cooling System Performance Affecting DPF. Particulate filter temperature sensor or regeneration condition fault. Stored as P2457-EXT.
fullDescription: Exhaust gas temperature (EGT) sensors fore and aft of the DPF tell the PCM whether regeneration temperatures are reached and that the substrate is not overheating. Exhaust Gas Recirculation Cooling System Performance Affecting DPF — stored as P2457-EXT. Loss of accurate temperature data forces the PCM to abort regen or, worse, allow runaway combustion that damages the substrate.
safetyImpact: Driveable but watch for excessive regen frequency or hot exhaust smell; severe over-temp can crack the DPF.

causes.cause: Failed EGT sensor (open or shorted)
Wiring damaged from exhaust heat
Connector corrosion
Sensor tip soot fouling
PCM calibration / software

fixSteps.title: Read EGT Sensor PIDs
fixSteps.instruction: Compare pre- and post-DPF EGT readings at cold start and after warm-up.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor pigtail for melted insulation or chafe near exhaust; repair as needed.

fixSteps.title: Resistance Test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure sensor resistance at ambient and compare to spec table.

fixSteps.title: Replace EGT Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Use anti-seize on threads; torque to spec and clear codes.

faq.q: Are EGT sensors reusable?
faq.a: No — once removed, the threads gall and accuracy drifts; always install new.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Short distance only; avoid towing and high load until repaired.

title: DPF Differential Pressure — Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High (P2460-EXT)
shortDescription: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High. DPF differential pressure sensor circuit fault. Stored as P2460-EXT.
fullDescription: The differential pressure sensor measures the drop across the DPF substrate, letting the PCM estimate soot load and trigger regenerations. Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too High — stored as P2460-EXT. A faulty signal masks real soot accumulation and either skips regens or forces them constantly, both of which damage the DPF.
safetyImpact: Driveable; incorrect soot estimation can over- or under-trigger regen, causing oil dilution or DPF saturation.

causes.cause: Soot or carbon plugging the pressure hoses
Cracked or pinched DP sensor hose
Failed differential pressure sensor
Wiring or connector corrosion at sensor
PCM software calibration outdated

fixSteps.title: Inspect DP Hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect both pressure lines and clear any soot blockage; check for cracks and proper routing.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Signal
fixSteps.instruction: With engine running, watch DP sensor PID at idle and under load; compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Verify Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check 5V reference, ground, and signal continuity from sensor to PCM.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install OE differential pressure sensor and clear codes; perform regen if soot load high.

faq.q: Can I clean the hoses myself?
faq.a: Yes — disconnect both ends, clear soot with a pick, and blow through with compressed air.

faq.q: Should I replace just the sensor?
faq.a: Replace only after confirming hose plugging is not the root cause.

title: Diesel Particulate Filter — Diesel Particulate Filter Soot Accumulation Severe (P2462-EXT)
shortDescription: Diesel Particulate Filter Soot Accumulation Severe. Diesel particulate filter (DPF) efficiency or regeneration fault. Stored as P2462-EXT.
fullDescription: Diesel particulate filters trap soot from exhaust and burn it off during regeneration cycles. The PCM monitors differential pressure across the filter, exhaust temperatures, and computed soot load. Diesel Particulate Filter Soot Accumulation Severe — stored as P2462-EXT. If left unaddressed the DPF can plug, triggering limp mode and forced dealer regeneration.
safetyImpact: Driveable; risk of forced regen failure, reduced power, and DPF replacement if soot loading climbs further.

causes.cause: Excessive soot loading from short trips
Failed differential pressure sensor or hoses
Faulty exhaust temperature sensor (EGT)
EGR or turbo issue causing rich combustion
DPF substrate damaged or saturated with ash

fixSteps.title: Read DPF Data
fixSteps.instruction: Pull soot load %, ash load, miles since last regen, and differential pressure values via scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Run Forced Regeneration
fixSteps.instruction: Command a static regen if soot load is within service range; monitor EGT and back pressure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pressure Sensor & Lines
fixSteps.instruction: Check differential pressure hoses for soot blockage, cracks, or moisture; test sensor signal.

fixSteps.title: Replace or Service DPF
fixSteps.instruction: Clean or replace DPF if substrate damaged, ash saturated, or regen fails.

faq.q: Can I clear the code without service?
faq.a: Clearing without addressing soot load returns quickly; force a successful regen and inspect sensors first.

faq.q: Will highway driving fix it?
faq.a: A 30 minute high speed run can complete a passive regen if soot load is moderate and EGT sensors are healthy.

title: Particulate Filter Temperature — Particulate Filter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1) (P246A)
shortDescription: Particulate Filter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1). Particulate filter temperature sensor or regeneration condition fault. Stored as P246A.
fullDescription: Exhaust gas temperature (EGT) sensors fore and aft of the DPF tell the PCM whether regeneration temperatures are reached and that the substrate is not overheating. Particulate Filter Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1) — stored as P246A. Loss of accurate temperature data forces the PCM to abort regen or, worse, allow runaway combustion that damages the substrate.
safetyImpact: Driveable but watch for excessive regen frequency or hot exhaust smell; severe over-temp can crack the DPF.

causes.cause: Failed EGT sensor (open or shorted)
Wiring damaged from exhaust heat
Connector corrosion
Sensor tip soot fouling
PCM calibration / software

fixSteps.title: Read EGT Sensor PIDs
fixSteps.instruction: Compare pre- and post-DPF EGT readings at cold start and after warm-up.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor pigtail for melted insulation or chafe near exhaust; repair as needed.

fixSteps.title: Resistance Test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure sensor resistance at ambient and compare to spec table.

fixSteps.title: Replace EGT Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Use anti-seize on threads; torque to spec and clear codes.

faq.q: Are EGT sensors reusable?
faq.a: No — once removed, the threads gall and accuracy drifts; always install new.

faq.q: Can I drive with this code?
faq.a: Short distance only; avoid towing and high load until repaired.

title: Crankcase Pressure — Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit (P226A-EXT)
shortDescription: Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit. Crankcase pressure sensor or PCV system fault. Stored as P226A-EXT.
fullDescription: Modern engines monitor crankcase pressure to detect blow-by, PCV system leaks, and oil separator faults. Crankcase Pressure Sensor Circuit — stored as P226A-EXT. Excessive crankcase pressure shortens seal life and oil leaks; insufficient pressure can indicate a broken hose or stuck valve.
safetyImpact: Driveable; ignoring it leads to oil leaks at front/rear main seals and accelerated turbo wear.

causes.cause: Failed PCV valve or oil separator
Cracked or detached PCV hose
Crankcase pressure sensor fault
Excessive blow-by from worn rings
Oil cap or dipstick seal leaking

fixSteps.title: Inspect PCV System
fixSteps.instruction: Check valve, separator, hoses, and dipstick seal for cracks and proper seating.

fixSteps.title: Smoke Test
fixSteps.instruction: Introduce smoke at the oil fill cap and look for escape points around hoses and gaskets.

fixSteps.title: Verify Sensor Signal
fixSteps.instruction: Read crankcase pressure PID with engine warm; compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace PCV valve, separator, or sensor as identified; clear codes.

faq.q: Is this serious?
faq.a: Not immediately, but unaddressed blow-by accelerates seal and turbo failure.

faq.q: Can I clean a PCV valve?
faq.a: Most modern PCV valves are sealed assemblies and should be replaced rather than cleaned.

title: NOx / Torque Limit — NOx Exceedence — Insufficient Reagent (DEF) (P2BAA)
shortDescription: NOx Exceedence — Insufficient Reagent (DEF). NOx aftertreatment fault triggering driver inducement / torque limit. Stored as P2BAA.
fullDescription: Diesel emission systems use NOx sensors and SCR (selective catalytic reduction) with DEF injection to meet emissions targets. When NOx output stays high or DEF dosing fails, the PCM enforces driver inducement strategies including torque reduction and eventual no-start. NOx Exceedence — Insufficient Reagent (DEF) — stored as P2BAA.
safetyImpact: Driveable initially; persistent fault enters inducement countdown and ultimately disables vehicle starts.

causes.cause: Failed NOx sensor (upstream or downstream)
DEF quality, level, or freezing issues
SCR catalyst aged or contaminated
DEF injector clogged or stuck
EGR fault elevating NOx output

fixSteps.title: Read NOx & DEF Data
fixSteps.instruction: Capture upstream/downstream NOx ppm, DEF level, dosing quantity, and SCR efficiency.

fixSteps.title: Verify DEF Quality
fixSteps.instruction: Test DEF concentration with refractometer; confirm fluid is OE-grade and not contaminated.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Dosing Module
fixSteps.instruction: Test DEF injector spray pattern and supply line pressure; clear crystallization.

fixSteps.title: Replace NOx Sensor or SCR
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed component; perform aftertreatment relearn / SCR adaption.

faq.q: Why is my truck losing power?
faq.a: It is in driver inducement mode — the system progressively limits torque and speed until the fault is repaired.

faq.q: Can I top off DEF to clear it?
faq.a: Sometimes — if the trigger was a DEF level or quality issue. Persistent codes need sensor or SCR work.
